text:
support-ops: FYI ACME reported a big p95/p99 regression on embeddings API in ap-south-2 starting ~02:10 UTC after last night's infra update. p95 ~60ms -> 420ms, p99 ~2.3s -> 5.6s. They say timeouts & intermittent 503s.
ajay: oncall looking. do we know what rolled last night? CUDA/driver/firmware?
support-ops: rollout notes show CUDA 12.3 + driver 535.XX on GPU pool, and a nvme firmware push to a subset of ap-south nodes.
lucas: can you paste a graph link?
support-ops: https://grafana.redwood/intruder/d/latency/embeds?orgId=1&var-region=ap-south-2 (private) — spike aligns with deploy.
maria: tagging @ajay and @lucas — customer is on a dedicated pool in that region, high qps, KV cache heavy workload.
ajay: ok first triage steps: 1) repro with small load against one affected node, 2) check iostat/disk latency, 3) check dmesg for nvme timeouts, 4) check kernel scheduler changes.
support-ops: running repro now with `wrk -t4 -c50 -d60s` hitting /v1/embeddings, will post results.
sre-bot: Deploy finished: cuda-12.3-driver-535 rolled to 60% at 02:05 UTC; nvme-fw-2.1.4 applied to 12 hosts at 02:08 UTC.
support-ops: repro results: throughput drops ~30%, tail latency jumps. iostat shows occasional very high await (hundreds ms).
lucas: can you paste `dmesg` around the spike?
support-ops: ```
[02:11:02] nvme nvme0: I/O 12345 QID 0 timeout, aborting
[02:11:02] nvme nvme0: reset controller (recovery)
[02:11:03] nvme nvme0: controller reset succeeded
[02:11:05] nvme nvme1: I/O 67890 timeout, aborting
```
ajay: that looks like NVMe resets -> host I/O stalls which would evict/pressure KV cache and increase GPU stall time. likely explains p99.
irma: customer says they saw the spike coincident with 'service errors' in their app logs. they're already on a support SLA call.
maria: mitigation proposal 1: roll back driver/firmware on the smallest impacted subset to see if latency recovers. 2: route ACME's traffic to eu1 as short-term fallback. 3: reduce batch size / set max_tokens smaller for ACME to reduce KV pressure.
lucas: also add IO QoS cap on their tenant VMs (throttle background GC/evict tasks), and temporarily increase KV cache reservation to avoid aggressive eviction.
ajay: agree. immediate steps I'm doing: - cordon 3 affected hosts from scheduler and drain; - trigger driver rollback manifest for drained hosts; - move ACME pool to standby hosts in ap-south that weren't patched.
support-ops: running cordon: `kubectl cordon gpu-host-037` and `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets` now — moving pods.
deploy-bot: rollback job started: driver-rollback-job-840123 triggered by ajay.
ajay: posting quick repro command for oncall if needed: ```sh
# run local repro against node
wrk -t8 -c100 -d30s http://10.2.12.45:8000/v1/embeddings
# collect iostat and dmesg
iostat -x 1 10 > /tmp/iostat.out
dmesg | tail -n 50 > /tmp/dmesg.out
```
support-ops: after moving ACME to standby hosts p95 dropped to ~80ms and p99 to ~420ms — much better. :thumbsup:
irma: confirmed phone call with ACME, they can tolerate short failover while we complete rollback. they want root cause analysis and ETA for permanent fix.
lucas: next: compare NVMe firmware versions and driver combos that were green in canary. run fio pattern repro to simulate KV cache warmup + random reads to see if driver+fw triggers reset.
ajay: engineering action items: - bisect: nvme-fw vs driver vs kernel changes; - test rollback state to confirm. expected ETA 3-6h to confirm and then schedule full rollback or patch.
maria: I'll draft customer update: we performed failover and we're rolling back the recent infra update in ap-south-2; investigating NVMe resets that caused host I/O stalls and increased tail latency. will follow up within 2 hours.
sre-bot: Alert suppressed for ACME pool: p99 alert auto-muted by incident handler.
deploy-bot: driver-rollback-job-840123 completed on 6 hosts, monitoring.
support-ops: monitoring: nodes with rollback show no more NVMe resets in last 10m, latency graphs trending down.
ajay: recommend we also add a preflight for future firmware/driver pushes: simulate KV-cache heavy workload + nvme stress to catch resets. file a postmortem once stable.
lucas: logging note — add more granular NVMe SMART/telemetry scraping to Prometheus so we detect timeouts earlier.
irma: customer is happy with temporary measures, wants a written RCA and mitigation plan.
maria: assigning follow-ups: @ajay (rollback verification + bisect), @lucas (test matrix + telem), @support-ops (customer comms), @maria (postmortem doc).
ajay: will add runbook steps to prevent accidental rollout overlap with firmware changes.
support-ops: thanks team, I'll keep this thread updated with any customer feedback. :pray:
